summary: An app can start, update and end a live activity with a title, a text line, an optional scheduled start and a stale time. The shell keeps the activities in a registry with a dismissal window and shows them as rows in its Notification Center widget area, but it draws no lock-screen or compact presentation, activities carry no custom views, and there is no remote start or update through push tokens. iPadOS 16.1 and later per the index.
rea_evidence: not captured: tools/parity/rea-page.sh reported 'no CDP browser on 127.0.0.1:9333 (run: tools/parity/rea-page.sh --start)'; facts are from tools/parity/docc.py

features.note: functions over the shell service that return an activity id; no typed Activity object and only the app that started an activity may update or end it
content is a title and a text line with a stale time; no typed state object
state is derived from the times, so no timer is needed; the registry is a pure model with host tests
start time is passed through; the shell side does not show a timed activity yet
an ended activity stays at most four hours; the dismissal options are the ones the model defines

features.feature: Notification Center presentation (lock screen and compact views missing)
features.apple: Live Activity views on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island
features.note: Notification Center's widget area shows one row per live activity on screen; there is no lock-screen view and no compact or expanded island presentation

features.apple: ActivityConfiguration, SwiftUI views for each presentation
features.note: content is text only; apps cannot supply layouts or regions

features.feature: Remote start, update and end with push tokens
features.note: no push token or server path for activities
no activity keys are read from the app manifest or the SDK on this branch
no update budget is enforced or relaxed for activities

features.apple: Launching your app from a Live Activity
features.note: no tap target on an activity

gaps: No lock-screen or compact presentation: activities appear only as rows in the Notification Center widget area.
Activities are text only; there is no custom layout per presentation.
No remote start, update or end from a server through push tokens.
No manifest declaration and no frequent-update budget.
No tap target that opens the app scene for an activity.
